notes.title: Secrets of the Gods Update
notes.notes:
The gods have revealed Becky's past in Harvest Island's new update, Secrets of the gods. A story that intertwines the fate of Will and Samantha in escaping Harvest Island. Key items found in ambiguous places that helped Will and Samantha during their escape is explained in Becky's fight for survival. Along with Harvest Island's extended ending, escape one last time as the gods have granted you this final journey's climax!

There's so much to write and I'm excited to share my news to everyone!

It's been over a month since the launch of Harvest Island. I have been really busy fixing a lot of issues and for the most part, everything is polished. It's day and night to how Harvest Island was first launch vs how it is now. There's so much more horror moments that'll scare you. I have to hold my breath to make sure I wouldn't get jump scare when I tested my own game. And there were times I did get scared because I wasn't paying attention.

Harvest Island is such a unique game because I wanted to challenge the expectations of the farming sim genre. By making it a horror, it creates a lot of new opportunities in the farming sim that most developer wouldn't explore in making. I wanted to focus on the storytelling, the dark tones (Especially the scary music and the Sound effects), and the emphasis on exploration - that's where the fun in the game is at.

There has been a lot of patches since the game's release. Over 60! The feedback that you guys have shared helped Harvest Island a lot. I've read so many reviews on steam, lurking on twitch and youtube, and took the time to address every critique I've heard. I can't stress enough how important that was for this game and it really helped. The improvements are all across the board. All-around balancing, expanding existing ideas, and adding more eerie horror moments.

It truly is like day and night to how Harvest Island is now vs how it was since released. I can't even begin to describe the amount of changes the game underwent. 

And finally, the extended ending. The journey of Harvest Island was left open ended. There wasn't an ending but a cliff hanger. Now, there is a proper ending. And as you reach that ending, you'll be extremely excited to know what the game has to offer in the future. I'll let you experience that instead of me telling you!

And! Another surprising news! I've added a story B to the game! Story A is Will and Sam which is the main story but B helps add more depth to story A. This pretty much elevates the writing a lot. Sometimes the game can be a slow start and it takes a while to get to the horror, which is the meat of the game, but with story B, it immediately starts, promising you to stick around until the very end and to experience Harvest Island's gripping story.

Lastly, I've introduced another god statue in your bedroom. This god statue gives permanent bonuses to help the game progress faster! It expands on the existing idea of God Idols and emphasizes the usage of it. This helps the game's balancing tremendously because now the game can be played in two ways. An adventure game without the farming aspect (Story Mode), or a farming sim (Normal Mode) that slowly turns into an adventure game and becomes the story mode in mid game.

I encourage everyone to try/play/revisit Harvest Island because Harvest Island is unique. It combines the extreme two genres together. And with the added new content, it elevates the writing to a new level. Harvest Island tells a compelling story that will stick with you for a very long time, even after you've finished the game. It's worth the play!

Yobob

The game now feels like a eerie horror game. It has a lot of horror elements. There are a few game design ideas that needs some time to develop before I implement them. Because the game is 25+ hours long, probably more and you have the freedom to explore wherever, these horror elements are far in between but are effective. One of the biggest issues is that gamers are impatient and really want the horror as soon as possible. The beginning of the game is bogged down if you don't care about the farming aspect and just want the horror/adventure. So, in the next few updates, I'll add more weird events to remind the players that the horror is just beginning but stick around for it to really happen.

notes.title: New Demo Update!
notes.notes:
Welp, since the day I announced my delay, a lot of progress has been made. A lot of polishing has been made and a lot of balancing as well. There's even a fast travel! Check that out!

This past two weeks has been hectic for me that I forgot to post a new demo for the indie fest. So, I've uploaded a new polished demo for you guys to take a look and play! Hopefully I'm not too late. I'll also upload a broadcast sometime soon this week as well for those of you that just want to quickly glance at the game and check out how it is. I'll talk about the game development in my broadcast.

As for the game update and how it's going. I would say it's 95% complete. I just need to wait on a bit more art, make a bit more music, and have a few more testers to play the final version of the game one last time. Very very very close to being done. In my next post, I'll give you a confirm release date of when Harvest Island can be played. It really will be released this year!

Here's the list of new things:
-Game scale (You can now zoom into the game 2x since people had a hard time seeing the game)
-Text box animated to come from sides
-Clear petting Objectives (This reduces confusion and helps balance the game when you feed, tend to the animals, and pet them)
-UI Art implemented
-Animals have Favorite foods (I'll let you figure the secret out :))
-New Heart Emoji
- New fish animation
-New coconut animation
- New bugs animation
- New Well watering Animation
- New cotton animation
- New apple tree animation
- Replaced a few old object arts (Like logs, twigs, mussels, apples)
-Refined part of the story's writing so that it doesn't feel repetitive.
- New Character Portraits (Lot's of new expressions added)
- Fast Travel added (There's an entire new world in that fast travel!)
- Balanced food consumption and energy consumption for "Tutorial" part.
- Extended the demo just a little bit more so that the game has a resolution and finishes the game's "Tutorial" and premise.
-Added 3 children's story books (Read it in the father's room once you journey along the game a bit)
-New Translations added (But this is a bit incomplete since I'm still working on this.)
-Added Nap Feature

There's probably a lot more which I can't remember from the top of my head since I'm just working purely in getting the final game released vs keeping the game updated to you guys. There's a lot of changes and I know you'll like them.

notes.title: Release Date Delayed
notes.notes:
Harvest Island will be delayed. The amount of work is enormous with just translating, testing, and polishing alone. I can't finish all of this in 3 weeks. I have given myself 2 months to do this and it's still not enough. Harvest Island will be be released between June-September

I am a very transparent developer and this is what I need to get done before the release.
Music - I need to add more music to the game.
Polishing - The game requires a lot of balancing. This means testers needs to replay the game every time I make massive changes to the game's balancing and this can take weeks to finish. The game also requires more cut scenes and more writing. The story is complete and written. That won't change, but the extra writing is for more world building and more character development. There is also new illustrations that needs to be fitted into the game as well and that can take a week or more to import and fit for each dialogue.
Translation - This is taking the most of my time this past two months. The amount of work to translate 6 languages is insane. I'm about maybe 50% done with this. Once that's done, there's the translation testing which hasn't even started because of the sheer amount of work from importing the translations work to the game AND programing the translations to fit in the game without causing any bugs/cut offs and other little annoying bugs that international players will face. I have tested my game in english but not other languages. Also keep in mind these translators are oversees and it takes roughly 16- 24h for them to respond which adds more time to the development.

I'm sorry that I have to delay the game, but it must be done. I do not want to publish a game that's filled with bugs, lack of polish, and subpar development. I've been pulling so many all nighters to make it to the release date but it's just impossible. The translators are struggling to meet deadlines due to unforeseen circumstances, there's not enough time for testing in their languages for better quality of translations, and there's just not enough time for me to test my game which most of the development time has been towards translations and fixing translations problems.

Two months is not enough time to finish all of these big tasks. I need more time to finish a game where you can enjoy playing.

The release date will be between June - September this year.

notes.title: Game Dev Progress Update - Potato farming in Indie Game Sucks
notes.notes:
Hi,

It's been a while but I have good news! I'm seriously starting a youtube channel to help promote Harvest Island more. This is a good thing for you because I'll be making Harvest Island Content! So, some of these content will reveal new areas in Harvest Island, but it's purely comical. Sometimes I'll post developer progress but most of the time, I just want to make you laugh. It's something I can do while developing Harvest Island at the same time since I know you guys have been waiting for this game for a long time. If you followed me in the super early stages, that's 2 years!

As for the game Harvest island. I know the biggest question is when will it be finished? Well, I have the entire game development road map planned out and I have a set date when I want to finish this game. This is pretty much what I have left to do to finish the game.

This is literally taken out of my notes from the big canvas I have written... But I'll explain more after you take a quick glance at it. (The sloppy writing is from me using a mouse lol)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37605883/6b569d2a7ed22969f0af6c95b3aaf6ea0908e01c.png[/img]

The main art which is all of the environmental art is 85-90% done.
The illustration is probably 20% done. This isn't a big deal since I have someone else working on these. So it shouldn't affect the release of the game.
Water tides is a code for me to say that, replace all the water in the game and be sure to add low tides and high tides. Pretty much a rework of the beaches in Harvest Island. This is maybe 10% finished. I still have to program a few things before the tides are final.
And then there's the secret animal map. That's pretty much is a secret :) But this is 0% done. If people have been following my dev log on my website, wild animals are really important.

Next we have Eventing. This just means to me that I have to create cutscenes for the game. Particularly the main story. And I'm talking about the ending of my game. So, you can say that the entire game's cutscenes is about 50% complete. The other 50% is the game's end game. This also implies other background programing I have to do like achievements, quests, and NPC Dialogue.

Story is 90% finished. All I have to do is write the game's lore. Which will take a while. And also write the the game's ending which is already planned out. I can't finish this without finishing the art so this will take a while for me to even start writing the game's ending. Plus there's the illustrations I have to wait on as well.

Testing. This is pretty much 0%. I have tested the game while I was developing it. So if things broke, I would fix it quickly, but small bugs that I wouldn't even think of testing would take some time for me to find them. Plus I'm going to find friends and have them play the game blindly. You can consider testing as polishing phase. Which will take a huge amount of time from me because I would be playing the game beginning to end like 100x to find bugs with different style playthroughs. And the game is pretty long and kinda open world. Would you even consider stardew valley open world? Well, you can say my game has the freedom to explore.

Easter egg island. That's just code for me to design the game's easter eggs. Yeah, it's pretty much self explanatory. If you guys played the beta, I'm sure you found game references. This island is pretty much answering those references. This is at 0% but I already have planned everything out for this.

And finally music. I'll be writing a lot of music. The game's music is probably 40%-50% done. Writing music is pretty quick for me unless I have to write a 5 min orchestral piece. We will see how my testers say about my music. If it's bad, I'm upping the level of music. If it's good, You can expect the game to release sooner. Also, I'm thinking about adding a singer which I already have lined up.

And that's pretty much everything currently with Harvest Island. So when will the game get released? I'm too afraid to give you the date because this is a lot of work, but I made deadlines for myself to finish. (Hopefully in a understandable time frame that doesn't kill me) This lets you peek into how soon Harvest Island will be finished and I hope that this is enough to keep you waiting.

And be sure to subscribe on youtube if you haven't yet!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37605883/22b1a4c2a4147bd3cf2bdcbe70bd47d409894201.png[/img]

notes.title: Harvest Island Demo Update Release
notes.notes:
It's been a while since my last update and everything is going fine. The game is still in development and continuing perfectly fine. So, I've decided to publish a demo on the main page of Harvest Island. It's an accumulation of what I have worked on so far. Unfortunately, it'll only be in English until the release of the game. The demo is about 30-40 min long. Harvest Island underwent through a lot of changes since the beta of the October Steam Festival. There are still a little bit more content I want to add before the release of the game so please be patient.

For those of you who have been following me since the beginning of my game development journey, thank you for sticking with me.

And in recent news to the Ukrainian crises, I have been watching it very closely. I know politics should not be in video games, but I want to offer my support to Ukraine in anyway I can and I think the world is changing which forces me to adjust my business. A lot has happened in the world and Russia and Ukraine are affected the most. Currently, there is no way I can translate to the Russian language as all payments exchanges are blocked. All communications are blocked. So, until the war is over, the Russian translations will not be in the final version of the game as a sign of protest. I'm sorry to the Russian people who were looking forward to Harvest Island. I blame the government. Not the people. I hope that one day the world can turn peaceful again and Russians who were looking forward to my game and other steam games can continue on with there lives normally without Putin.

Bravery to Ukraine. Bravery to the people. Bravery to those who support.
